prose: Microsoft unveiled the Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI chip built on TSMC's N2P process, designed as the 'primary AI inference system' for Microsoft's products and services - including the latest reasoning models and agentic tasks. Production rollout starts in 2027.

Microsoft's Scott Guthrie claims Maia 300 will deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems, and up to 7x the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200 in a full 96-accelerator configuration. The endgame: scaling the Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments so Microsoft relies mainly on its own silicon instead of Nvidia and AMD.
highlights: Maia 300: Microsoft's third-gen in-house AI chip on TSMC N2P.
Claimed 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems.
Up to 7x Maia 200's rack-scale throughput in a 96-accelerator config.
Production rollout in 2027; aimed at reasoning models and agentic tasks.
Goal: multi-gigawatt Azure Maia deployments, less Nvidia/AMD reliance.
